subject: Air-gapped bonding: GitOps peering + Helm shim interoperability review
messages:
From: Alice Greene <alice@nimblehealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-12T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Kickoff: air-gapped bonding + GitOps peering (initial deploy plan)

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is our high-level deployment plan and an initial network diagram for the air-gapped site (see nimble-deploy-plan.pdf and airgap-peering-diagram-v2.png). We want Redwood to review the proposed GitOps peering approach and the Helm "shim" strategy we plan to use to avoid reaching out to external registries from the air-gapped clusters. Key asks:

- Confirm whether Terraform VPC peering + on-prem bonding will work with your dedicated control-plane proxy pattern.
- Any red flags in the proposed Helm chart shimming and image import flow (we plan to push images to an internal registry and use a signed registry mirror).
- CI/CD flow: can the Redwood private agent run the validation pipeline in the isolated network, or do we need an additional jump-host for artifact staging?

We'd like a short review today if possible and can join a call tomorrow morning PST.

Thanks,
Alice Greene
DevOps Manager, NimbleHealth
alice@nimblehealth.com

Attachments:
- nimble-deploy-plan.pdf (application/pdf)
- airgap-peering-diagram-v2.png (image/png)

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Alice Greene <alice@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-12T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: air-gapped bonding + GitOps peering (initial deploy plan)

Alice — thanks for the docs, I skimmed the diagram and plan. High-level notes below (quick turn so we can sync):

1) VPC peering vs. bonded WAN link
- Peering looks feasible for the cloud side; for on-prem we recommend a dedicated bonded interface (BGP) back to the Redwood edge to ensure predictable egress and metrics tagging.
- Action: can you confirm the expected MTU and whether the on-prem team can publish BGP neighbor ASN? That affects our traffic-engineering snippets in Terraform.

2) Helm shim strategy
- The overall approach (internal registry + signed mirror) is good and aligns with our air-gap patterns. The key gap is chart provenance: we need a signed chart provenance file and an immutable artifact store.
- We propose a small shim chart that replaces remote image refs with local registry refs during the release pipeline (pre-render step). See attached helm-shim-proposal.md for an example pre-render hook.

3) CI/CD in air-gapped env
- Redwood private agent can run validation inside the isolated network, but it requires an outbound control channel to our control-plane proxy (TLS-over-mTLS). If policy forbids any outbound, we need a jump-host in the DMZ to mediate artifact transfer.
- Recommendation: allow a single egress to controlplane.redwood.internal:443 via an allowlist and mTLS cert pinning.

4) Evidence & compliance
- For SOC-style evidence, please include artifact signing keys and a list of registry mirrors we will trust. We can generate a short checklist for your compliance team.

We'll do a 30m call tomorrow at 10:30 PST to walk these points unless you prefer earlier.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com

Attachments:
- helm-shim-proposal.md (text/markdown)

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, Alice Greene <alice@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-12T14:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: air-gapped bonding + GitOps peering (initial deploy plan)

Sergio / Alice — quick CI notes from my review:

> On 2027-01-12 11:05, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com wrote:
> > The key gap is chart provenance: we need a signed chart provenance file and an immutable artifact store.

Agree with Sergio. A couple of pragmatic points for the pipeline:
- The pre-render hook to rewrite image refs should be an idempotent step and produce a deterministic artifact (checksum). Add a step to store the checksum in the release metadata so we can trace back.
- We need to avoid running helm repo add (external) during rendering. Use a local index.yaml mirrored into your internal registry.
- For Ansible/agent bootstrap, include a fallback where the private agent can run in a read-only mode (validation only) if the artifact copy step fails — we should fail safe and not attempt to alter clusters unintentionally.

I'll paste a short pipeline fragment in the call. Also: Dylan, we should surface this as a "validation-only" pipeline job in our shared templates.

— Neha Kapoor
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Subject: commercial constraints for airgap deployments

Alice, Sergio — two quick constraints from procurement/legal that will impact the pipeline:

- We need a signed mutual NDAs addendum for on-prem data handling (I can drop a short template).
- If Nimble requires our agents to run in an air-gapped environment under customer-managed HSM, we must align on support SLA — that typically moves to enterprise support and changes the standard MSA.
- Any third-party registry or artifact tooling that is "enterprise licensed" (e.g., Harbor with a paid support bundle) must be declared in the BOM before we start agent deployment.

Please have Nimble confirm whether they will use an off-the-shelf mirror (e.g., Harbor) or a homegrown registry; that affects our ops runbook and the licensing clause.

Thanks — happy to discuss on the call.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
